plan: [With 3 bidders and a third-price rule, the symmetric equilibrium solves ∫_0^v b(m) dm = v^2, giving b(v)=2v. This strategy maximizes expected profit against opponents using the same rule. My private value is v=20, so the equilibrium bid is 2*20 = 40. I will bid $40 (allowed in $0.1 increments) to maximize long-run expected profit.]

[I have value $29. With two opponents whose values are iid uniform on [0,49], if they bid their values then P(win)=(b/49)^2 and E[min|win]=b/3, giving EU maximized at b=2v but truncated at the support. Since 2·29>49, bid the upper support to secure the item. This maximizes expected profit. ]

[Third-price means winner pays the lowest (third) bid. Bidding above my value can increase chances to win but risks paying more than my value if both opponents overbid, causing losses. No prior history to predict opponents, so bid my true value to avoid systematic overpayment while capturing profitable wins when the lowest rival bid <45. This is conservative and maximizes long-run expected profit under uncertainty. ]
